beats.label: S1 · Moiraine takes the villagers
beats.text: Moiraine, an Aes Sedai hunting the reborn Dragon, comes to the Two Rivers. A Trolloc raid drives Rand, Mat, Perrin, and Egwene to flee with her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the premise and pulls the whole group onto the road — every subsequent arc begins from this uprooting.

beats.label: S1 · Shadar Logoth splits them
beats.text: The group scatters through cursed Shadar Logoth. Mat pockets a tainted dagger, Perrin — who killed his wife in the raid — begins hearing wolves, and Egwene proves she can channel.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Every villager's ongoing arc — Perrin's wolves, Mat's dagger, Egwene's channeling — is planted in a single scene.

beats.label: S1 · Nynaeve, Logain, and gentling
beats.text: Nynaeve tracks the group and heals a wounded Moiraine, displaying raw One Power beyond Liandrin — the Red who has just severed the false Dragon Logain from the source.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nynaeve enters the story, and Logain's gentling shows what the Aes Sedai do to male channelers — the fear that shapes every choice Rand makes next.

beats.label: S1 · Siuan's staged exile
beats.text: Moiraine and her secret lover Siuan, the Amyrlin, stage a public exile so Moiraine can take the villagers to the Eye of the World. Mat, held by the tainted dagger, stays behind.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Siuan's covert alliance is the political cover for the Dragon hunt; Mat being left at Tar Valon opens him to Ishamael.

beats.label: S1 · Fal Dara and the Horn
beats.text: At Fal Dara, Egwene, Nynaeve, and three others link their channeling to destroy a Trolloc army — the effort burns most of them out. Perrin finds the Horn of Valere in the ruins.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Horn is what Perrin and the Shienarans spend next season chasing, and Nynaeve's raw One Power is why the Shadow will target her.

beats.label: S1 · Rand is the Dragon
beats.text: At the Eye, Rand rejects the Dark One and reveals himself as the Dragon Reborn. Fearing male channeling will drive him mad, he begs Moiraine to keep the secret and vanishes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Everything that follows hinges on Rand in hiding, Moiraine's silence, and the fact her power was severed protecting him.

beats.label: S1 · Fain flees, ships land
beats.text: Padan Fain, a Darkfriend who led the Trollocs to the villagers, steals the Horn. Off the western coast, great foreign ships arrive carrying channelers of unknown intent.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Horn in Fain's hands and the unnamed channeler-army on the shore are the two threats that ignite the next season.

cliffhanger.text: Rand is the Dragon Reborn, gone into hiding and terrified of the madness in the male One Power. The Horn of Valere is in Darkfriend hands, and huge foreign ships bearing channelers have just landed on the western shore.
questions: Can Rand stay hidden — from the Aes Sedai and from the taint on saidin?
Where is Padan Fain taking the Horn, and who does he really serve?
What do the foreign channelers on those ships want?

characters.name: Rand al'Thor
characters.line: The Dragon Reborn, hidden after the battle at the Eye — terrified the male One Power will drive him mad.

characters.name: Moiraine Damodred
characters.line: The Aes Sedai whose connection to the One Power was severed by the Dark One at the Eye of the World.

characters.name: Lan Mandragoran
characters.line: Moiraine's Warder and the exiled heir of a fallen kingdom, now Nynaeve's lover.

characters.name: Egwene al'Vere
characters.line: A Two Rivers girl with strong channeling ability, headed to the White Tower to train.

characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara
characters.line: The village Wisdom with raw One Power greater than any Aes Sedai — blocked, only channels in fear or rage.

characters.name: Perrin Aybara
characters.line: Killed his wife in the raid, hears wolves he can't explain, and briefly held the Horn of Valere before Fain took it.

characters.name: Mat Cauthon
characters.line: Corrupted by a tainted dagger from Shadar Logoth, refused the last leg of the journey and stayed at Tar Valon.

characters.name: Siuan Sanche
characters.line: The Amyrlin Seat of the White Tower and Moiraine's secret lover, publicly staging her exile as cover.

characters.name: Padan Fain
characters.line: The lifelong Darkfriend who led the Trollocs to the Two Rivers and now has the Horn of Valere.

characters.name: Liandrin
characters.line: A Red Ajah sister who gentled the false Dragon Logain — openly disdainful of anyone she cannot control.

beats.label: S2 · Ishamael runs Liandrin
beats.text: Ishamael, freed servant of the Dark One, chooses to watch Rand rather than kill him. He turns Liandrin — secretly Black Ajah — against Rand's friends inside the White Tower.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ishamael becomes the season's chief antagonist, and Liandrin's Black Ajah loyalty is the reveal every Tower plot swings on.

beats.label: S2 · Seanchan take Perrin
beats.text: Perrin joins Shienarans hunting the Horn, but a Seanchan invasion captures them. The Seanchan collar channelers as slaves, and Ishamael appears to bend Perrin toward the Shadow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Seanchan and the damane leash — the practice that shapes the Falme climax and Egwene's captivity.

beats.label: S2 · Selene is Lanfear
beats.text: In Cairhien, Rand falls for an innkeeper named Selene — who is Lanfear, a returned Forsaken determined to have him. Moiraine stabs her, but Lanfear survives.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Lanfear steps into the story as the Forsaken who drives every remaining Rand plot in the show.

beats.label: S2 · Damane handoff
beats.text: Liandrin hands Egwene, Nynaeve, and the princess Elayne to the Seanchan as damane. Egwene is leashed and broken by her sul'dam Renna; Nynaeve and Elayne escape into Falme.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets every hero on a collision course at Falme and marks Egwene with an experience that hardens her from here on.

beats.label: S2 · Mat, Min, and the prophecy
beats.text: Rand, Moiraine, and Lan race to Falme. Mat, held by Ishamael and warned by Min's vision that he will spear Rand, tries to stay away — but Lanfear drags him there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Min's prophecy into position to pay off, and shows Mat losing agency to the Shadow players around him.

beats.label: S2 · Egwene kills Renna, Mat blows the Horn
beats.text: In Falme, Egwene strangles Renna with her own collar. Backed into a corner, Mat is forced to blow the Horn of Valere and summons the Heroes of legend as their captain.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Egwene's kill is her turning point, and blowing the Horn irreversibly binds Mat to it as its living champion.

beats.label: S2 · The Dragon named, Forsaken loose
beats.text: Ishamael tricks Mat into wounding Rand, but Moiraine breaks his shield and Rand kills him. Falme names Rand the Dragon Reborn. Moghedien warns Lanfear all Forsaken walk free.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Dragon is public and the Forsaken are loose — the two facts that frame every next-season conflict.

cliffhanger.text: Rand has been proclaimed the Dragon Reborn before an entire city, still bleeding from Mat's spear. Ishamael is dead — but Moghedien has just told Lanfear that every one of the ancient Forsaken now walks free.
questions: Which of the newly-freed Forsaken will move against Rand next, and how?
Now that Lanfear knows she is not alone, whose side does she really choose?
Can Rand — untrained, wounded, and publicly marked — survive with every enemy of the Light hunting him?

characters.name: Rand al'Thor
characters.line: The Dragon Reborn, publicly declared before Falme after killing the Forsaken Ishamael — wounded through the side by Mat's spear.

characters.name: Moiraine Damodred
characters.line: Aes Sedai whose connection to the One Power has been restored, back at Rand's side after months in hiding.

characters.name: Lan Mandragoran
characters.line: Warder to Moiraine again, having been briefly cut off from her when she released him earlier in the season.

characters.name: Egwene al'Vere
characters.line: A freed damane, hardened by Renna's collar and by the killing she used to escape it, still a novice at the Tower.

characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara
characters.line: Newly raised as Accepted, still blocked from channeling except when angry or afraid.

characters.name: Perrin Aybara
characters.line: Confirmed as a Wolfbrother now bonded to a wolf pack, and killed a Whitecloak commander in a rage at Falme.

characters.name: Mat Cauthon
characters.line: Freed of the tainted dagger and marked as the champion of the Horn of Valere, still haunted by past-life memories.

characters.name: Min Farshaw
characters.line: The seer whose vision of Mat spearing Rand keeps her wary, now openly with the group.

characters.name: Lanfear
characters.line: An ancient Forsaken who tried to seduce Rand into the Shadow — wounded by Moiraine, alive, and still obsessed.

characters.name: Liandrin
characters.line: Exposed as Black Ajah after handing three of her own novices to the Seanchan on Ishamael's orders. Fled the Tower.

characters.name: Moghedien
characters.line: A newly-revealed Forsaken who has just informed Lanfear that every one of the ancient Shadow lords now walks free.

beats.label: S3 · The Black Ajah, exposed
beats.text: A month after Falme, Siuan exposes Liandrin as Black Ajah in open court. A battle erupts as more sisters reveal themselves; Liandrin escapes the Tower with her allies.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Black Ajah is now a public enemy and Liandrin is loose — the shape of every Tower and Tanchico plot this season.

beats.label: S3 · Three roads
beats.text: Rand, Moiraine, Egwene, and Lan head to the Aiel Waste with Aviendha; Perrin returns to the Two Rivers; Nynaeve, Elayne, Mat, and Min head for Tanchico.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The three-way split defines every subplot of the season and separates our heroes from each other for the whole run.

beats.label: S3 · Rhuidean's history
beats.text: In Rhuidean, Rand walks his ancestors' memories: the Aiel were pacifist servants of the Aes Sedai, and Lanfear was the Aes Sedai who first freed the Dark One from his prison.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes Lanfear as the world's original sin and gives Rand the Aiel's true history — the leverage he'll use to claim them.

beats.label: S3 · Nynaeve breaks her block
beats.text: In Tanchico, Nynaeve breaks her channeling block cornering Liandrin. Liandrin escapes with an artifact that enslaves male channelers and offers it to Moghedien to use on Rand.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nynaeve's block is finally gone, and Moghedien and Liandrin now hold the leash meant for Rand's neck.

beats.label: S3 · Perrin holds the Two Rivers
beats.text: Perrin defends the Two Rivers from Trollocs led by Padan Fain. He spares Fain, is hailed lord by the villagers, and hands himself to Whitecloak Dain Bornhald as promised.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Perrin ends the season as titled lord of a village he's just saved — and as a Whitecloak prisoner by his own promise.

beats.label: S3 · Elaida takes the Tower
beats.text: Elaida of the Red Ajah seizes the White Tower. Siuan is branded a Darkfriend and executed, leaving the Tower hostile to Rand and Nynaeve's group cut off from support.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rand loses his one great institutional ally and gains an actively hostile Aes Sedai power at his back.

beats.label: S3 · Lanfear turns, Couladin rides
beats.text: Rand rejects Lanfear. She wounds Moiraine, allies with the Forsaken Rahvin, and props Couladin up as a fake Car'a'carn. Rand claims his Aiel by summoning rain on the Waste.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Lanfear switches from suitor to enemy and a rival Dragon rides against Rand — the two forces that will hunt him next.

cliffhanger.text: Rand has been named Car'a'carn of the Aiel — but Couladin rides against him as a fake Car'a'carn, backed by Lanfear and the Forsaken Rahvin. Elaida rules a White Tower openly hostile to him, and Liandrin holds an artifact that can leash him at Moghedien's word.
questions: Can Rand defeat Couladin and Rahvin before his own Aiel are turned against him?
What will Elaida's Tower do to the Dragon they cannot control?
Will Liandrin get her leash around Rand's neck before Nynaeve can catch her?

characters.name: Rand al'Thor
characters.line: The Dragon Reborn, now acknowledged as Car'a'carn of the Aiel after walking his ancestors' memories in Rhuidean.

characters.name: Moiraine Damodred
characters.line: Back at Rand's side with her power restored, wounded again in the final duel with Lanfear.

characters.name: Lan Mandragoran
characters.line: Warder to Moiraine, still tied to Nynaeve across the distance between them.

characters.name: Egwene al'Vere
characters.line: Accepted of the Tower, now training in the World of Dreams with the Aiel Wise Ones.

characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara
characters.line: Accepted who has finally shattered her channeling block by cornering Liandrin in Tanchico.

characters.name: Perrin Aybara
characters.line: Newly hailed Lord of the Two Rivers, held prisoner by the Whitecloaks under his own surrender bargain.

characters.name: Mat Cauthon
characters.line: Given three wishes by an inhuman Eelfinn, left with foreign memories and pieces of his own life missing.

characters.name: Lanfear
characters.line: The Forsaken who once freed the Dark One — rejected by Rand, she has turned on him and joined Rahvin.

characters.name: Liandrin
characters.line: Deposed head of the Black Ajah on the run, holding an artifact that can enslave a male channeler.

characters.name: Moghedien
characters.line: The Forsaken who has quietly steered the season's disasters, now allied with Liandrin to leash Rand.

characters.name: Elaida
characters.line: A Red Ajah who has just seized the White Tower and executed Siuan — openly hostile to the Dragon.
